title: MIRI implementation rule
description: How one committee-defined check is verified. A rule names an operator and gives it arguments; it may NEVER restate a definition-owned field (weight, level, severity, category) - additionalProperties: false makes that a schema error, not a quiet override. Worth comes from the vendored definition and nowhere else, so a re-pin of the standard re-weights every implementation without touching a rule.

check.description: The committee check this rule verifies. Must be active in the vendored registry; the loader refuses it otherwise.

rule.description: The operator and its arguments. Argument shapes are declared per operator in operators-v1.json and validated there; this schema only fixes that an operator is named.

proof.description: The evidence this rule can fail. A rule with no failing proof is a rule nobody has proven can fail - the vacuous-pass class the committee has catalogued five times.

allOf.description: A declarative document rule is a new execution path and ships failing fixtures. A native rule wraps an implementation the suite already pins. A cli.invoke rule's proof is its own expect block, executed live against the subject on every selfcheck run; expect.minProperties keeps it non-vacuous.
